back: Globular; 2 α + 2 β globin chains; 4 haem groups each with Fe²⁺; carries up to 4 O₂.
Hydrophilic R groups on the outside of the molecule.
A non-protein group permanently bound to a protein and needed for its function (e.g. haem).
Glycine at every third position (Gly–X–Y, often with proline and hydroxyproline).
Its tiny R group (H) fits in the centre of the triple helix so chains pack tightly.

front: What gives collagen its tensile strength?
back: Triple helix with hydrogen bonds; covalent cross-links between molecules; staggered fibrils bundled into fibres.
Tendons, skin, bone, cartilage, artery walls, cornea.
Valine replaces glutamic acid at position 6 of the β chain.

front: Haemoglobin v collagen in one line?
back: Haemoglobin: globular, soluble, 4 chains + haem, transport. Collagen: fibrous, insoluble, 3-chain triple helix, strength.
